title: Southwest State Election: Speaker Madobe Wins Presidency 88-1 Amid Fraud Allegations, Rival Withdrawal
detail: Somalia's House of the People Speaker Sheikh Aden Mohamed Nur Madobe won the Southwest State presidential election in Baidoa, defeating Abdiasis Mohamed Sheikh Osman Jawaari 88 votes to 1 (one ballot invalid) among 90 lawmakers. Leading contender Sharif Hassan Sheikh Aden withdrew beforehand, alleging the electoral commission and acting president had broken an agreed no-mobile-phones-in-the-hall rule meant to protect ballot secrecy. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud congratulated Madobe, who is widely seen as the federal government's preferred candidate and must relinquish the parliamentary speakership under constitutional dual-office rules. Critical Threats' Africa File characterized the outcome as the FGS's 'handpicked candidate' winning 'amid fraud allegations,' deepening opposition claims that federal member state elections are being engineered from Mogadishu.

media.caption: Hiiraan Online (Jun 10, 2026): Somali Speaker wins Southwest State presidency election after rival withdraws
